findings_and_open_policy_questions.classification: Existing 059 q1345 historical open same-source/home question with new bounded 95e evidence; no new finding or unique-count change
findings_and_open_policy_questions.trace: At 95e Open includes checked source, origin, span and rect. If source and home match, MapState::open updates only rect; the existing MapPose retains its span, yaw, origin and home_span. Reset restores the old home_span. The browser mount sends the supplied span on opening; the inspected ordinary strategic producer emits a constant 60,000m initial span. Thus a different supplied span is ignored in this branch, but a supported varying-span producer, desired reopen/reset policy, and stale city/presented transitions have not been established.
findings_and_open_policy_questions.conditions: A subsequent supported Open for the same source and home carries a different intended span or should deliberately reset prior pose. Preserving prior user interaction may instead be intended; no user-visible outcome or runtime behavior observed.
findings_and_open_policy_questions.future_direction: Specify resume versus replacement and reset semantics at the owner; if a supported new requested home span must be honored, carry it through the existing state transition while preserving intentional user pose and source-switch invalidation. Trace retained city/surface and callers before deciding.

findings_and_open_policy_questions.classification: New bounded current source policy question, not a proven product defect or accepted unique count
findings_and_open_policy_questions.trace: After each non-city command, the receiver sets state.failure to result.err(). A source-mismatched environment or source/revision-rejected overlay takes the Ok path without replacing data, so if any earlier operation returned Err and a later accepted or ignored Ok command is applied before the next Last status publication, the latter clears that error before that status serializes it. City uses a separate early dispatch. Status reads the current failure; a successful command may intentionally indicate recovery.
findings_and_open_policy_questions.conditions: An actual supported error-producing map operation and subsequent Ok command must both apply before a status snapshot. Whether a failure should survive a later command, command order and observer timing, and any actual consequence remain open. No command, scheduler, browser or status was executed.
findings_and_open_policy_questions.future_direction: Determine the intended lifetime and acknowledgment of operation errors. If a failure must be observable, retain a typed outcome or sequence until the responsible observer can see it, without treating deliberate stale-input no-ops as successful new data or changing valid recovery semantics.
findings_and_open_policy_questions.historical_relationship: Related to, but not automatically identical to, 774 RIG-ROOT-ADM03-193, whose historical receiver read explicitly records result.err() and asks about stale-input feedback. No previous finding ID has been established as an exact alias.

findings_and_open_policy_questions.classification: Conditional representation/admission question; actual internal bypass and supported harm unproved, no new unique count
findings_and_open_policy_questions.trace: Only the Open/Resize Serde fields call viewport(), which requires positive extent, finite nonnegative offsets, full dimensions at least extent and crop end at most full dimension plus one pixel. The enum and raw CanvasRect fields are crate-visible, while CanvasRect itself derives Deserialize and has public fields; the compiler-visible type alone therefore does not guarantee the map-specific check for every hypothetical internal construction or other shared canvas route.
findings_and_open_policy_questions.conditions: A real non-decoding MapCommand Open/Resize producer would have to construct or pass a bad rectangle, or another shared CanvasRect route must rely on the map guarantee. No such producer or malformed command was established; exact-name source search is not proof of absence. Map camera currently also uses max(1) in some denominators. The shared strategic route is separately scoped.
findings_and_open_policy_questions.future_direction: Trace all supported command constructors and distinguish checked map viewport from the intentionally raw shared canvas port; enforce the appropriate single admission owner only if the guarantee is required beyond decoder use.
findings_and_open_policy_questions.historical_relationship: ROOT-ADM-G073 and Rig dependency-qualification-116 explicitly distinguish MapCommand custom admission from the shared raw CanvasRect/StrategicView path. The prior strategic subpixel candidate is related by shared producer/receiver but has a distinct trigger and has not been proved an alias.
